Subject: Re: Request: BYO HSM deployment constraints and approval path

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing to cut over our internal LLM inference environment into a VPC-connected private deployment and need a compact, auditable plan for the keystore portion. Specific asks from our side:

- Minimum network egress requirements for Redwood's keystore agent and any telemetry endpoints (we need to allowlist CIDRs).
- A clear rotation cadence recommendation for HSM-wrapped KEKs vs. application-level data keys (what should Acme rotate and what does Redwood manage?).
- A rollback matrix for operator errors (operator proxies, unseal failures, HSM connectivity loss) with contact/approval gates.
- Evidence artifacts we can attach to our audit (signed attestation, KMS logs, signed operator manifests).

Can you send a compact playbook and a one-page sign-off matrix we can take to our security committee? We need something by Friday PDT if possible.

Thanks,
John Miller
Infrastructure Security Lead | Acme Corp

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sealed keystore HA rotation and minimal-egress playbook

John —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a first-pass playbook and the rollbacks sheet (see attachments). Below is a concise summary and the approval/rollback gates we recommend for Acme. If that aligns, we'll finalize the PDF and provide the signed attestation package.

Summary:
- Minimal egress: allowlist outbound to: telemetry.redwood.ai:443 (TLS) and ocsp.redwood.ai:443 for cert revocation checks; outbound to 3 IPs that host our control-plane for attestation handshake. We will provide exact CIDRs in the CSV attachment (network-whitelist-cidr.csv). No other egress should be required.
- Key ownership and rotation: Acme retains KEKs in your HSM (BYOK). Redwood suggests:
  - KEK rotation: annual or on-incident (customer-controlled; Redwood provides wrapped-key rollover tooling).
  - Data key (DEK) lifecycle: generated per-instance by Redwood runtime, rotated every 30 days by default and re-wrapped with the current KEK.
- Secrets handling: operator proxies run in customer VPC; only wrapped keys and signed attestations traverse network. Plaintext keys never leave HSM or sealed keystore memory.
- HA and unseal: two operator instances across AZs, automatic re-seal on connectivity loss >120s and manual approval for forced unseal.

Rollback & approval matrix (high level):
- Operator install misconfig (config drift): rollback to previous container image; approval: engineering manager (Acme) + Redwood ops on call.
- Unseal failure (HSM unreachable): automatic reattempts 3x, then re-seal; approval required for manual unseal (Acme security engineer + Redwood security).
- KMS connectivity loss with degraded decrypts: fail closed for writes, read-only mode for reads for up to 2 hours; after 2 hours, failover plan to warmed standby (requires both parties' approval).

Next steps:
1) Can your security team confirm the three CIDRs in network-whitelist-cidr.csv?
2) If yes, we'll finalize the playbook PDF and provide the signed attestation bundle and a DocuSign link for the sign-off matrix.

I'm attaching: redwood-byo-playbook-v1.pdf, network-whitelist-cidr.csv, rollback-matrix.xlsx.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Kim — quick notes inline.

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 6:14 PM kimberly.park@redwood.ai wrote:
> - Minimal egress: allowlist outbound to: telemetry.redwood.ai:443 (TLS) and ocsp.redwood.ai:443 for cert revocation checks; outbound to 3 IPs that host our control-plane for attestation handshake.

Two clarifications:
1) Telemetry is optional for hardened environments. We'll provide a telemetry-off profile; in that mode we do health pings only to the control-plane IPs (no stack traces, no prompt payloads).
2) For OCSP you can optionally use your internal OCSP proxy — we'll accept that if your proxy validates cert stapling at the operator.

Rotation cadence question: we recommend customers set KEK rotation to "on-demand or annual" but document the exact re-wrap procedure we run in the playbook. Suggest changing the DEK default to 14 days for higher-security profiles (we can offer 30/14 toggles).

Rollback matrix suggestion: add an explicit "operator eviction and zeroize" step for stolen or compromised operator credentials — outline steps to rotate KEK and reprovision sealed keystore with a new operator set. That step should require exec-level approval from Acme (security lead) + Redwood head of security.

I'll fold these into v1.1 if John confirms the CIDRs.

-tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions Engineering, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
